anomalies.obs: On the bottom bus connector J2 the +3V3 arrow is attached to pin 1 and PORTB1 is on pin 9. On the top bus connector J1 the +3V3 arrow is instead attached to pin 9 (the PORTB1 position) and pin 1 is left as the unconnected generic 'PIN1', so the two connectors no longer share the same pin-to-net map.
anomalies.exp: The specification requires J1 and J2 to carry 'identical nets on both so the board can be stacked', with +3V3 on pin 1 and PORTB1 on pin 9 of BOTH connectors. On J1, +3V3 must be on pin 1 and pin 9 must remain PORTB1.

evidence.quote: J1 / J2 ... identical nets on both so the board can be stacked between the M5Stack Core and a lower module (pass-through). Carries +5V, +3V3, BAT, GND, GPIO/UART pins
J2 left column: '+3V3' arrow at pin 1, 'PORTB1' at pin 9; J1 left column: '+3V3' arrow at pin 9, pin 1 labelled 'PIN1'

anomalies.impact: The board's +3V3 net is driven onto J1 pin 9 (the M5Stack PortB GPIO line) instead of pin 1, shorting a supply rail to a GPIO and leaving the M5Stack's 3V3 pin floating at the top connector; the pass-through of PORTB1 to the lower module is also broken. The stacked M5Stack would not receive 3V3 through J1 and the PortB signal would be clamped to 3.3V.

parsed.summary: All component values, types and polarities match the specification, but the top bus connector J1's pin-to-net mapping for +3V3/PORTB1 does not match the bottom connector J2, contradicting the spec's requirement that the two connectors carry identical nets; this appears to be a mis-wired/tampered pin assignment that would short +3V3 to a GPIO and break the 3V3 pass-through.
